notes: Identity independently verified from canonical text: title Avoiding overhead aversion in charity; authors Uri Gneezy, Elizabeth A. Keenan, Ayelet Gneezy; Science 346, 632–635 (2014), DOI 10.1126/science.1253932. This is a primary published main report with cover sheet and adjacent next-article material after references. Supplementary methods/text/table S1 are referenced but not included. No PDF supplied, so no rendering performed. Only n_o and es_value_o are assigned; other fields/sides are placeholders. Study 1 identifies the laboratory experiment but not one of several tests. Candidate recruitment N=449 is not promoted to analytic N. No N sum or df-based inference performed. Candidate comparisons: 5% uncovered versus no overhead, z=0.98, P=0.33; 50% uncovered versus no overhead, z=3.27, P<0.01; 50% uncovered versus 5% uncovered, z=2.32, P=0.02. Printed probit estimated marginal effects: 24% or 17% less likely for 50% overhead versus no overhead or 5% overhead, respectively. Further candidates: 50% covered versus no overhead, z=0.29, P=0.77; 50% covered versus 50% uncovered, z=3.00, P<0.01. Requested OR is not printed in the inspected main-text laboratory results; no odds ratio derived. No candidate selected without a contrast locator. Marginal-effect evidence: overhead treatment are 24% (or 17%) less likely ... to choose charity: water compared with those in ... the no-overhead (or 5%-overhead) treatment.
